Its single-step denoising error at σ ≥ 32 Å stays near the posterior-mean \"blob\" solution, and the sampler collapses. This is not a sampler bug: an oracle denoiser recovers the native exactly with the same sampler. The failure follows from the learning problem. To denoise a noisy cloud, the network must implicitly estimate the rotation that best explains it, a global, highly nonlinear computation that a transformer has to learn from augmented examples. The same network then folds the complex at 200 steps and reaches sub-2 Å accuracy at 600–800 steps. This matches a lesson from geometric deep learning (`paper_002`): building a symmetry into the model is far more sample-efficient than learning it from augmentation.
